facts.text: Londra Palace Venezia has been welcoming travellers since 1853.
facts.excerpt: Londra Palace Venezia has been welcoming curious independent travellers since 1853

facts.text: The hotel is a short stroll from San Marco.
facts.excerpt: A short stroll from San Marco, it is both elegant salon and private retreat

facts.text: The hotel has a rooftop altana terrace.
facts.excerpt: with its rooftop altana terrace just made for romance

facts.text: Rooms use Venetian materials such as brocade, silk, prized wood and marble.
facts.excerpt: The Venetian materials may be opulent – brocade, silk, prized wood and marble – but the effect is light, intimate, playful

facts.text: Motifs borrowed from historic Veneto villas decorate the walls and floors of the rooms.
facts.excerpt: Motifs borrowed from historic Veneto villas waltz over the walls and dance a pas de deux across the floor.

facts.text: Classic Room City View rooms look over the city's rooftops, ancient lanes, churches and bell towers.
facts.excerpt: enjoy intimate views of the city’s rooftops, ancient lanes, churches and bell towers

facts.text: Classic Room City View rooms have a view over the city with no lagoon view.
facts.excerpt: View over the City of Venice (no lagoon view)

facts.text: The Deluxe Room Lagoon View With Balcony rooms are on the second floor with Romeo and Juliet balconies facing the lagoon.
facts.excerpt: All located on the hotel’s second floor, these delightful double rooms offer 'Romeo and Juliet' balconies with front-row views of the lagoon.

facts.text: The Junior Suites include two rooms dedicated to past guests Tchaikovsky and D'Annunzio.
facts.excerpt: they include two rooms dedicated to illustrious past guests Tchaikovsky and D’Annunzio

facts.text: Each Junior Suite Lagoon View has a view of the lagoon and the island of San Giorgio.
facts.excerpt: each with its own captivating view of the lagoon and the island of San Giorgio

facts.text: The Suite Jules Verne is named after the French writer, who stayed at the hotel in 1884.
facts.excerpt: As original and inventive as the great French writer after whom it is named – who sojourned at the hotel in 1884

facts.text: The Suite Borges is dedicated to the Argentine writer Jorge Luis Borges and has Fortuny lamps and Murano vases.
facts.excerpt: Precious Venetian design details including Fortuny lamps and Murano vases adorn a suite that feels like an apartment

facts.text: The Top Floor Suite has a very large terrace with a view from the San Marco Basin to the Grand Canal.
facts.excerpt: It has a very large terrace, from which the view extends from the San Marco Basin to the Grand Canal, until reaching the roofs and bell towers of Venice

facts.text: Rooms have marble-lined bathrooms.
facts.excerpt: Marble-lined bathroom with bath or walk-in shower

facts.text: Guests can dine on the terrace as the sun sets over the lagoon city.
facts.excerpt: Will it be dinner on the terrace, as the setting sun turns the lagoon city into a fairy-tale vision?

facts.text: The LPV Bar serves signature cocktails.
facts.excerpt: this enchanted evening must surely begin with a signature cocktail in our LPV Bar

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler reports Tchaikovsky stayed in 1877 and wrote his fourth symphony as he surveyed San Giorgio Maggiore.
facts.excerpt: Tchaikovsky stayed in 1877, and wrote his fourth symphony as he surveyed San Giorgio Maggiore across the water.

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler says the property is a member of the Relais & Chateaux association.
facts.excerpt: the property is now a member of the Relais & Chateaux association

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler says the roof terrace is one of the highest in Venice.
facts.excerpt: The roof terrace is one of the highest in Venice and the view is divine.

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler says the lagoon-side Riva degli Schiavoni has become overrun with crowds and souvenir stalls.
facts.excerpt: In recent times the Riva has become overrun, though, and the crowds and schlocky souvenir stalls make these hotels feel like a calm refuge
